macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds toward $64,000 after Coldcard exploit and Strategy sales pressure
items.summary: Bitcoin rose roughly 1.6% over 24 hours and briefly climbed to about $64,160 as markets digested a confirmed Coldcard wallet exploit and recent Bitcoin sales by Strategy. Analysts said spot ETF flows were mixed, with outflows last week followed by inflows on the latest reported day.

items.title: Coldcard hack confirmed to have stolen more than 1,596 BTC
items.summary: A reported exploit of Coldcard hardware wallets was confirmed to have caused losses above $100 million, with 1,596 BTC stolen. The incident renewed focus on custody and wallet security risks across the crypto market.

items.title: Strategy sells 3,588 BTC, putting future corporate Bitcoin sales in focus
items.summary: The Block reported that Strategy sold 3,588 BTC, prompting analysts to watch whether more corporate Bitcoin selling follows. The sale added pressure to sentiment around one of the largest public Bitcoin holders.

items.title: European Commission reportedly looks to expand MiCA to cover tokenization and non-EU stablecoin issuers
items.summary: The Block reported that the European Commission is considering extending MiCA to address tokenization and stablecoin issuers outside the EU. If pursued, the move would broaden the bloc's crypto regulatory perimeter.

items.title: Sen. Wyden urges Senate leaders to preserve blockchain developer protections in crypto bill
items.summary: The Block reported that Sen. Ron Wyden asked Senate leaders to keep contested protections for blockchain developers in a broader crypto bill. The proposal highlights ongoing debate over how U.S. law should treat software developers and protocol contributors.

items.title: Binance Wallet adds Plume yield vault with access to Invesco and Bitwise funds
items.summary: The Block reported that Binance Wallet expanded its offerings by adding Plume's yield vault, which provides access to funds from Invesco and Bitwise. The development reflects continued growth in on-chain distribution of traditional asset products.

items.title: BNB outperforms as market cap rises and liquidations jump
items.summary: CryptoRank said BNB led gains among major assets, rising to about $591 while the total crypto market capitalization climbed to roughly $2.18 trillion. The same recap said 24-hour liquidations surged to about $224 million, signaling elevated trading stress.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent inside ChatGPT designed to carry out tasks across apps and files, signaling a push deeper into professional productivity tools. The launch intensifies competition with other enterprise AI offerings.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-Live voice models for real-time conversation
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The release expands OpenAI's multimodal capabilities and targets more natural conversational AI.

items.title: Meta opens developer access to Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released preview access to Muse Spark 1.1 for developers, alongside an upgraded model version. The move positions Meta more directly against Anthropic and OpenAI in paid AI model access.

items.title: Elon Musk's xAI releases Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: xAI launched Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model yet and emphasizing improvements for coding and agentic workflows. The company is marketing it as a cheaper, more efficient rival to leading frontier models.

items.title: Anthropic adds former Fed chair Ben Bernanke to Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, the oversight body intended to keep the company aligned with its public mission. The addition underscores growing governance scrutiny around frontier AI labs.

items.title: Meta announces major Canada data center buildout for AI infrastructure
items.summary: Meta said it will build a large data center in central Alberta, its first in Canada, to expand computing capacity for AI. The investment reflects the continuing industry trend toward massive infrastructure spending.

items.title: OpenAI copyright dispute escalates with sanction request from newspaper group
items.summary: A group led by The New York Times asked a federal court to sanction OpenAI over alleged misrepresentations about its ability to search systems for evidence tied to copyrighted journalism. The case adds to the legal pressure on AI training practices.

items.title: Italy fines Character.AI owner over data protection breaches
items.summary: Italy's data protection authority fined Character Technologies, the owner of Character.AI, for breaches of data protection rules. The penalty highlights rising regulatory scrutiny of consumer AI products in Europe.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox reportedly in major restructuring, with layoffs and studio cuts
items.summary: Microsoft’s gaming division is facing another round of layoffs, with reports saying Xbox is cutting about 3,200 jobs and dropping four game studios as part of a broader restructuring. The move is being framed as a major reset after a stretch of disappointing performance and strategy concerns.

items.title: IO Interactive to close a studio after Xbox pulls funding for an unannounced project
items.summary: IO Interactive, the developer behind Hitman and 007: First Light, is shutting one of its studios after Xbox reportedly withdrew funding from an upcoming project. The decision is expected to affect an unknown number of employees.

items.title: PlayStation pushes ahead on digital-only direction for new PS5 games
items.summary: Sony is continuing its shift away from physical media, with reports saying all new PS5 games will soon be digital-only. That move has fueled fresh criticism from fans who prefer disc ownership.

items.title: PlayStation’s physical-disc controversy continues as fans react to its latest messaging
items.summary: PlayStation followed up its recent “killing discs” discussion with a wireless fight stick promotion, prompting more backlash from players worried about the company’s stance on physical releases. The reaction reflects ongoing concern about the future of boxed game ownership.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass growth reportedly far below Microsoft’s expectations
items.summary: A new report says Microsoft expected Game Pass to reach about 77 million subscribers by now, but the service is believed to have around 30 million instead. Xbox leadership has reportedly acknowledged that the strategy has not delivered the growth Microsoft wanted.

items.title: Fortnite and GTA Online dominate recent release and update chatter
items.summary: Recent coverage highlights The Kortz Center Heist as GTA Online’s final major update before GTA 6, while Fortnite leaks and collaboration rumors continue to drive discussion about upcoming seasonal content. These remain among the most closely watched live-service developments in gaming.

items.title: Palworld 1.0 update confirmed with no price increase
items.summary: Pocketpair has confirmed that Palworld’s 1.0 launch will not come with a price hike, despite the game’s growth and upcoming full release. The announcement comes as the game passes a major player milestone.

items.title: Esports headlines center on MSI and regional competition updates
items.summary: The latest esports coverage features MSI match results, including Hanwha Life Esports falling to BLG and dropping into the lower bracket. Additional regional tournament news includes SOOP’s global Cross-Regional Fall Guys event and ongoing roster and interview coverage across major leagues.

items.title: Nintendo-related news includes Switch 2 and platform transition rumors
items.summary: Recent gaming news mentions Nintendo-related developments such as Switch 2 coverage, including reports tied to third-party releases and platform transition plans. The broader conversation also includes speculation about old-gen Switch discontinuation in some regions.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Meta plans its first data center in Canada
items.summary: Meta announced a 1GW data center in Alberta that it says will cost about $9 billion and take two to three years to build. The project is part of the company’s broader infrastructure expansion.

items.title: Apple loses EU court challenge over App Store and iOS gatekeeper designation
items.summary: The EU General Court dismissed Apple's legal challenge to its designation as a Digital Markets Act gatekeeper for the App Store and iOS. The ruling keeps Apple under the EU's platform rules.

items.title: India removes import duties on some smartphone and electronics parts
items.summary: India scrapped import duties on selected parts used to make mobile phones and other electronics, removing 7.5% and 5% levies. The move could lower costs for manufacturers such as Apple and Xiaomi.

items.title: Apple expands Broadcom chip-supply deal
items.summary: Apple said it will spend more than $30 billion under a new chip-supply agreement with Broadcom. Broadcom will also expand a factory in Colorado as part of the deal.

items.title: EU backs temporary rules to help platforms remove child sexual abuse material
items.summary: EU lawmakers backed reinstating temporary rules that would let platforms such as Google and Meta detect and remove child sexual abuse material. The proposal is intended to bridge a gap while longer-term policy is developed.

items.title: Coinbase restores prediction markets trading after outage
items.summary: Coinbase said it restored prediction markets trading after a technical issue disrupted the service. The restoration ends the outage for users of the platform.

items.title: Blue Origin reportedly seeks first outside funding at $130 billion valuation
items.summary: Reports say Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin is raising $10 billion in its first external funding round, with a pre-money valuation of about $130 billion. The round would mark a major shift for the rocket company.

items.title: Nvidia market value falls sharply as chip stocks sell off
items.summary: Nvidia reportedly lost about $1 trillion in market value in less than two months and is down 16% from its May all-time high. The stock is now trading at 18 times forward earnings, its lowest level since 2019.
